production.note: US model years. Acura's model chronology lists the third-generation Integra Sports Coupe and Sports Sedan for 1994-2001 with the GS-R's '1.8-liter 16-valve VTEC® inline 4-cylinder, 170 hp @ 7600 rpm, 128 lbs-ft @ 6200 rpm (GS-R)' from 1994 ('GS-R with VTEC® available in sedan for first time', 1994) and GS-R updates through 2000; '2001: Floor mats standard on all models; final model year'.

body.note: Acura's 1994 sheet lists the body styles as 'Coupe' and 'Sedan'. The GS-R coupe is chassis code DC2; the GS-R sedan is DB8. The record's weight is the coupe's.

aspiration.note: Inferred: Acura's sheet describes a DOHC VTEC inline 4 with no forced induction.

drivetrain.note: 'Transverse-mounted front engine/front-wheel drive with equal-length driveshafts'

transmission.note: '5-speed manual'. Acura's 1994 sheet lists the 4-speed automatic only for the RS and LS; the GS-R was manual only.

powerHp.note: Quote: "170 hp @ 7600 rpm (GS-R)" (SAE net). Acura's model chronology gives the same '170 hp @ 7600 rpm' for the GS-R in both bodies across the 1994-2001 generation (acura-chronology).

weightLb.note: GS-R coupe, 5-speed manual, 1994 model. Quote: "2667 lb (1210 kg)". The GS-R sedan is '2765 Ib (1254 kg)' (sic, the sheet's 'Ib' is 'lb').
